record: EVAL attempt 1 -- INCIDENT, not a scientific result
status: INCIDENT_RECORD -- frozen before the real attempt was launched
WHAT_HAPPENED: The eval process was killed mid-run by a shell-level `timeout 3000` (50 minutes) that I wrapped around the launch command myself, compounded by an identical 50-minute ceiling passed to the Bash tool's own timeout parameter. Neither ceiling was long enough: at ~31 sec/episode for 192 sequential single-environment episodes, the full run needed roughly 100 minutes. The process was killed at 18:27:11 UTC, mid-way through the z1|B cell.
ROOT_CAUSE: Operator error in MY OWN launch command, not a defect in the eval script, not an environment fault, not a model or treatment problem. Verified: GPU idle afterward (2187 MiB used, 1% util), disk not full (18.5 GiB free), no Windows Application-log crash entry, no leftover run lock. All consistent with a clean kill signal, not a crash.

WHAT_WAS_SEEN_BEFORE_THE_KILL.artifact_written: NONE -- neither ORACLE_GATED_K2_EVAL_RESULT.json nor the rows CSV exists

WHY_THIS_DOES_NOT_COMPROMISE_THE_ONE_SHO.the_scripts_own_guard_never_fired: eval_oracle_gated_k2.py refuses to run if OUT.is_file(). That file was never written, so the guard was never triggered and a genuine one-shot attempt has not yet occurred.
WHY_THIS_DOES_NOT_COMPROMISE_THE_ONE_SHO.no_model_or_treatment_change_was_possibl: The checkpoint under test was already frozen and sha256-verified before this attempt started (ORACLE_GATED_K2_MODEL_FROZEN.json, commit 417ef37f). Three win-rate point estimates offer no mechanism to alter a model that was fixed and hashed before they were seen -- there is no tuning knob they could have informed.
WHY_THIS_DOES_NOT_COMPROMISE_THE_ONE_SHO.what_was_NOT_seen_is_the_part_that_would: The gate is delta_A.lcb95 > 0 AND delta_B.lcb95 > 0. Neither delta, neither bootstrap interval, and no verdict were observed. The quantity the frozen criterion actually judges was never exposed.
WHY_THIS_DOES_NOT_COMPROMISE_THE_ONE_SHO.disclosed_rather_than_hidden: Per project discipline, this is recorded rather than quietly relaunched and forgotten. The next attempt is the genuine one-shot EVAL.

FIX_BEFORE_RELAUNCH: No shell-level or tool-level timeout will be imposed on the relaunch. The script runs to natural completion or genuine failure, whichever comes first.
DOES_NOT_ALTER: ORACLE_GATED_K2_EVAL_SPEC.json, the frozen gate, or the model under test
classification_is_not: a scientific result of any kind

CORRECTION_EVAL_IS_NOT_UNTOUCHED.the_correction: EVAL can no longer honestly be described as 'untouched'. Three point estimates were seen. The accurate statement is: EVAL PARTIALLY OBSERVED due to infrastructure timeout; no adaptive action permitted or taken.
CORRECTION_EVAL_IS_NOT_UNTOUCHED.why_this_matters: 'Untouched' would have been a convenient overstatement. The honest record is that the seal was broken by accident, that what was exposed is precisely enumerated, and that nothing was changed in response.

THESE_THREE_NUMBERS_MUST_NOT_BE_INTERPRE.rule: No interpretation of the partial point estimates is permitted before Attempt 2 completes. Reasoning about them now would convert an accidental peek into an adaptive analysis.
THESE_THREE_NUMBERS_MUST_NOT_BE_INTERPRE.worked_example_of_the_trap: z1|A (0.5938) exceeding z0|A (0.5625) may LOOK concerning for the crossover hypothesis. But the frozen gate is a PAIRED delta with an LCB95 criterion, not a comparison of marginal point estimates. Drawing a conclusion from the latter would be exactly the substitution the frozen criterion exists to prevent.
THESE_THREE_NUMBERS_MUST_NOT_BE_INTERPRE.what_is_permitted: reporting the numbers as an incident record, which is what this file does

ATTEMPT_2_CHANGES_NOTHING.the_only_difference: no artificial time ceiling, so the calculation can finish
ATTEMPT_2_CHANGES_NOTHING.no_fresh_eval_block: Not required and not used. The timeout was infrastructure failure, not a scientific decision, and no hyperparameter or checkpoint can change in response to what was seen.
